headline: A 2021 law moves parts of four North Carolina counties, including the Fort Bragg and Camp Mackall areas, from the Middle federal court district to the Eastern district.
what_it_does: The law changes the borders of two federal judicial districts in North Carolina. It moves portions of four counties that include the Fort Bragg Military Reservation and Camp Mackall from the Middle District to the Eastern District. Federal cases from those areas would now go to the Eastern District's courts.

who_it_affects.group: People living in the moved portions of the four counties
who_it_affects.how: Federal lawsuits and criminal cases arising there are now handled by the Eastern District rather than the Middle District.

who_it_affects.group: Parties and lawyers with federal cases from the affected areas
who_it_affects.how: They would file and appear in Eastern District courts for cases from these areas.

who_it_affects.group: Military personnel and families at Fort Bragg and Camp Mackall
who_it_affects.how: Federal court matters arising on those installations would go to the Eastern District.

when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not state an effective date. The law was enacted on July 6, 2021.
